Looking at my land and what I know from farming here my whole life, the answer is simple. My father grew wheat and corn on this land. My neighbors grow wheat and corn. I grow wheat and corn. That's how it's done in Quzhou.

I have about 8 mu of land. Every winter I plant wheat, every summer I plant corn on the same fields. The wheat feeds the family and the corn I can sell or feed to pigs. I don't take risks with new crops I don't know. When the seed seller at the market comes around, I'll buy whatever improved wheat seed he recommends — the kind everyone else is using — and the Zhengdan 958 hybrid corn seed like I always get. Hybrid corn always outyields the old varieties, I know that much.

For fertilizer, I put down urea and compound fertilizer. Maybe a bit more than I should, my wife says, but better too much than too little — I can't afford a bad harvest. I irrigate the wheat four times: once in winter to protect the roots from cold, once at jointing, once at heading, once more if it's dry at grain fill. Corn gets one or two waterings if August is dry. I use rotary tillage before planting wheat. For corn I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble — saves time and fuel.

Pesticides: I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring and do a fungicide spray near heading. For corn I spray once for stem borers if I see them. Not much more than that.
